chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abduwayh ibn Amir and others, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all of them from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When Ismail was born, Ibrahim carried him and his mother upon a donkey, and Jibrail came with him until he placed him at the location of the Hijr, and with him was some provisions and a waterskin containing some water. The House in those days was a red hillock of mud. Ibrahim said to Jibrail (peace be upon him): 'Is it here that you were commanded?' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: And in those days, Mecca was covered in Salam and Samur trees, and around Mecca in those days were people from the Amalekites.
And in another narration from him as well, he said: When Ibrahim turned to leave, Hajar said: O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us? He said: I am leaving you both to the Lord of this House.

He said: So when the water ran out and the boy became thirsty, she went out until she ascended al-Safa and called out: Is there anyone kind in the valley? Then she descended until she came to al-Marwa and called out similarly. Then she turned back to her son, and behold, his heel was kicking in water. So she gathered it, and it accumulated — and had she left it, it would have flowed away.

key_terms.البنية: The Building — a name for the Ka'ba, emphasizing its divinely sanctioned construction
key_terms.الحجر: Al-Hijr — the semicircular enclosure adjacent to the Ka'ba, marking where Ismail was initially placed
key_terms.الصفا والمروة: Al-Safa and al-Marwa — the two hills between which Hajar ran, now ritualized in the Hajj Sa'i
key_terms.العمالقة: Amalekites (Amaliq) — a pre-Islamic Arab people who inhabited the region around Mecca
key_terms.ربوة حمراء من مدر: A red hillock of mud — the primitive state of the Ka'ba site before Ibrahim's construction

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq narrate about the story of Ismail, Hajar, and the origin of Sa'i in Mecca?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the foundational story of Mecca: Ibrahim brought the infant Ismail and his mother Hajar to the barren location of the future Ka'ba, guided by Jibrail, who confirmed this was the divinely appointed site. The hadith preserves vivid historical details — the site was then just a red mud mound, surrounded by acacia trees and the ancient Amalekite people — giving context to Ibrahim's surrender to divine will. The account also narrates Hajar's desperate search for water between Safa and Marwa, and the miraculous appearance of the Zamzam water beneath the infant Ismail's heel, explaining the religious rite of Sa'i performed in Hajj to this day.
